1. Governance, accountability and risk
Policy governance, accountability, risk tolerance and acceptable use

NDIA must govern all ICT digital experience capabilities through approved investment, assurance and risk arrangements. Accountable owners must document risk tolerance, compliance obligations, exceptions and escalations, and all staff and contractors must use ICT resources properly, ethically and in support of NDIA functions.
The NDIA must clearly own and govern every digital experience capability. ICT must be used lawfully, ethically and for NDIA business, with risks, exceptions and decisions recorded.

2. User-centred services and transactions
User-centred service design, access model, connected journeys and digital transactions

Digital services must have a clear purpose, defined user groups, evidence-based user needs, a documented service offering and a channel/access model. Service teams must connect related channels and partners, record access decisions, and support legally effective electronic transactions, communications, signatures and approvals with retained evidence.
The NDIA must design digital services around real user needs, make access choices clear, connect related channels, and keep evidence for valid electronic transactions.

3. Inclusion and accessibility
Inclusion, accessibility, multilingual access and channel choice

NDIA digital services, content, identity proofing and workplace technologies must be inclusive and accessible. They must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA where applicable, use plain and culturally appropriate communication, support language services and reasonable adjustments, and provide assisted or non-digital options where users need them.

The NDIA must make digital services, content and workplace technology accessible and inclusive. People must have language support, reasonable adjustments and assisted or non-digital options when needed.

4. Content, publishing and trust
Content quality, official identity, proactive publication and rights management

NDIA public and internal digital content must be clear, consistent, trustworthy, discoverable and correctly branded. Publishing teams must meet web content, publication, FOI/IPS, annual reporting, copyright, licensing and third-party content obligations before release or reuse.
The NDIA must publish digital content that is clear, accurate, current and officially branded. Content must be approved before release and reused only when rights are clear.

5. Privacy and protected information
Privacy, personal information, protected Agency information and identity privacy

NDIA must manage personal information, protected Agency information and identity data using privacy-by-design. Digital services must minimise collection, give clear notices, use or disclose information only as authorised, secure information, support access and correction, manage overseas processing, complete PIAs where required and maintain privacy governance, training and registers.
The NDIA must protect personal, identity and protected Agency information by design. Collect only what is needed, explain why, use or share it lawfully, secure it, and support access and correction.

6. Information sharing and data transparency

9. Supplier and procurement controls
Supplier, procurement, contract and third-party risk controls

NDIA must assess supplier and procurement risk before engaging providers for digital experience, collaboration or EUC services. Contracts must include enforceable security, privacy, access, assurance, incident, exit, subcontractor, foreign-control and value-for-money obligations, and supplier compliance must be monitored for the life of the arrangement.
The NDIA must check supplier and procurement risks before buying or using digital services. Contracts must clearly require security, privacy, access, incident, exit and assurance controls.
